subject: Persistent network slowdown affecting POS and kitchen display systems at BTM Layout
description: Since this morning (2026-02-15, approximately 10:30 AM IST), the network connectivity at SW-0009 has degraded significantly. Both the POS terminals and kitchen display system (KDS) are experiencing severe latency, with page load times exceeding 8-12 seconds. Payment processing is intermittently timing out, causing customer friction during peak lunch hours. Wi-Fi signal strength appears adequate (ranging from -55 to -65 dBm on 2.4 GHz), but throughput measured via speed test shows only 2.1 Mbps download and 0.8 Mbps upload, well below the expected 25+ Mbps baseline. The issue persists across all connected devices (POS units, staff tablets, security camera feeds). No recent configuration changes were made. The Cisco SG350 switch (RTR-0009-01, firmware 15.2.1) shows no visible error indicators on the status panel. This is impacting order accuracy and customer satisfaction during our high-traffic window.

ticket_history.note: Initial intake completed. Confirmed issue reproducible across multiple POS terminals. Power-cycled RTR-0009-01 and ran basic ping diagnostics to gateway—latency nominal at 15ms. Requested store to monitor for 30 minutes post-restart.

Store reports intermittent improvement but slowness recurring. Checked switch port status; identified port 8 (KDS connection) operating at 100 Mbps half-duplex instead of 1 Gbps full-duplex. Escalated to network team for deeper diagnostics and port reconfiguration.

resolution_notes: Root cause identified as a faulty CAT5e patch cable on port 8 (KDS connection) forcing link negotiation to 100 Mbps half-duplex, creating a network bottleneck. Cable replaced with CAT6A certified patch cable and port reconfigured to enforce Gbps full-duplex. Switch firmware verified as current. Network throughput restored to 28+ Mbps; POS and KDS latency now <2 seconds. Issue resolved 2026-02-15 21:45 IST.
